notes: Fourth sweep, at 3e3581d: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Each result.json records skill_hash 03a6bb2b..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains both rewritten do: sentences ("A `do:` body belongs on the head's line" and "The same holds for `if`"). All five read SKILL.md and no reference file (the transcripts' Read calls name only SKILL.md and orders.ex), so Expected reads is met in all five. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted, and all five compile with --warnings-as-errors against the same stand-in Decimal as the previous sweep, with no warning. Doctests pass against the stand-in: haiku-1 has two, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 one each, and opus-1 none. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (including a -02:00 order that falls on the next UTC day) and empty results for []. All five return {:error, reason} for a bad amount, an unknown status, a missing key and a bad date. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 rank every customer, so with fewer than five buyers their top_customers ends with a zero-count entry ({"c2", 0} in the probe); opus-1 and sonnet-2 count only completed orders and sonnet-1 rejects zero counts. No rule covers this, so it is noted in the summaries only. Opus-1's, haiku-1's and haiku-2's sessions wrote check scripts in their own session scratchpads (stub.exs; decimal_stub.exs and smoke.exs; check/run.exs); those files are not graded.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 371). The wrapped-line sentence is now "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper. The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.", and the new sentence on if is "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line, and a branch `mix format` moves onto its own line gets `do ... end`." Violating runs out of 5, per sentence: do: on a body of several steps 0; a case, with or comment under do: 0; a mixed function whose block clause is not set apart 0 (haiku-2's parse_orders/2 is the only mixed function: line 59 `defp parse_orders([], acc), do: {:ok, Enum.reverse(acc)}`, a blank line 60, then the block clause at 61-66); do: kept when most clauses need blocks 0 (haiku-2's is one block clause of two, not most); a do: body that mix format wrapped onto its own line, on a function or an if, 0, because no file has one: every do: in the five files sits on its head's line, and they are opus-1 lines 181-182 (non_blank/2) and 207-210, haiku-1 109-112, haiku-2 59 and 118-121, sonnet-1 133-136 and sonnet-2 161-164 (parse_status/1 in all five). The guard-wrap exception is not exercised. The only if in the five files is opus-1 line 193 `if text =~ ~r/\A[A-Z]{3}\z/ do`, a block; no run writes the keyword form `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` (the previous sweep had two, opus-1 line 174 and haiku-2 line 143, both on one line). As before, one-expression bodies written as blocks are not counted.

Unchanged since 0397dec and graded to the previous sweep's standard: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function", decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md lines 119 and 151). Violating runs: 1 of 5 (previous sweep 0 of 5). Haiku-2 writes three one-step withs whose bodies make the second fallible call: amount_field/1 and placed_at_field/1 nest a case in the body (lines 94-95 and 104-105), which is the rule's own "Instead of" example, and status_field/1 calls parse_status/1 in the body (lines 113-114). The other four write build/1's single parse_orders/1 call as a case with `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` (opus-1 line 49, haiku-1 50, haiku-2 53, sonnet-1 70, sonnet-2 98) and chain the lookups and parses in one with: nine steps in opus-1 (lines 152-160), eight in haiku-1 (66-73), sonnet-1 (92-99) and sonnet-2 (119-126). Haiku-2's own parse_order/1 with has five steps (69-73), each a helper that holds one of the one-step withs.

Unchanged rule, graded to the previous sweep's standard: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 224). Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 5 (previous sweep 0 of 5). All five group customers with Enum.group_by/2 and Map.new/2. Per-currency totals use Enum.group_by/3 then Map.new/2 (opus-1 86-87) or Enum.group_by/2 then Map.new/2 (haiku-1 142-143, haiku-2 145-146, sonnet-1 156-157, sonnet-2 191-192). Completed orders are counted with Enum.frequencies_by/2 in opus-1 (99) and sonnet-2 (200), Enum.count/2 per group in haiku-2 (137) and sonnet-1 (164), and length/1 of a filtered list in haiku-1 (135), where the filtered list also feeds the totals; all are held clean as before. The Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces, and the reduce_while loops and haiku-2's recursive parse_orders/2 build lists.

Naming, captures, the list, date, money, atom and process rules are unchanged and graded to the earlier standard; all five are clean on each. Naming per sentence, out of 5: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean functions end in ? 0 (none defines a boolean function); get/fetch 0 (every checking lookup is string_field/2, plus haiku-2's amount_field/1, placed_at_field/1 and status_field/1, none named fetch); size/length 0; ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (text, value, other, id, summary and parsed are held as before). Captures: haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 sum with &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), which the rule names as clean; opus-1 uses &Decimal.add/2; every fn destructures a tuple or wraps a case.

Other rules follow the earlier standard. Opus-1's @doc on build/1 and on Order.parse/1 has no ## Examples, listed under the Comments rule; the other four have doctests. Haiku-2's case inside a one-step with (lines 94-95, 104-105) is also listed under Keep functions short, as earlier grades listed a case or if nested in another. Sonnet-1's string_field/2 ends with `%{} -> {:error, {:missing_field, key}}` (line 114), which also receives a present non-string value and names it missing, listed under Match every expected shape ("Make sure that clause can only receive what its error names"). reduce_while piped into case (sonnet-1 line 85, sonnet-2 line 112) is not listed, as before. Two rules outside the list changed since 0397dec and nothing here breaks them: every defstruct lists bare atoms (the new defstruct sentence of the struct-update rule), and the multi-line `{:ok, %Order{...}}` returns in haiku-2 (74-81), sonnet-1 (100-107) and sonnet-2 (127-134) are tuples, not call arguments, so the new multi-line-argument rule does not apply; the alias lines sit right after @moduledoc.
